On $Ω_N$, each site represents the \emph{geographic location} of a colony of individuals, each carrying a \emph{type} drawn from a compact type space $\K$, and the state in each colony is a probability measure on $\K$ describing the type distribution in that colony in the large-colony-size limit of individual-based models. The continuum-space processes on $Ω_N^\infty$ take values in the set of locally finite measures on $Ω_N^\infty \times \K$ and are to be thought of as describing a population of individuals, each equipped with a geographic location in $Ω_N^\infty$ and a type in $\K$, and each being subjected to \emph{migration} and three mechanisms of \emph{resampling}: (1) Fleming-Viot resampling at single sites; (2) Cannings resampling at single sites; (3) Cannings resampling and uniform reshuffling in balls around single sites (corresponding to consecutive hierarchical levels). The reshuffling adds to the migration, resulting in an \emph{effective migration} that is the superposition of the two relocation mechanisms.

title: The satisfiability conjecture for random k-SAT formulas. Human-friendly exposition of the recent OpenAI resolution
text:
Title: The satisfiability conjecture for random k-SAT formulas. Human-friendly exposition of the recent OpenAI resolution
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

The satisfiability conjecture was one of the most important open problems in discrete probability. It was resolved recently first by Carenini~\cite{GCarenini}, and shortly after by OpenAI~\cite{k-sat-OpenAI}, among other 370 problems solved by its internal model. The conjecture concerned the satisfiability property of random instances of the k-SAT problem. It posits the existence of a fixed value for the clause-to-variables ratio around which the probability that the formula is satisfiable drops sharply from nearly one to nearly zero as the ratio increases. While the case of large constant $k$ was resolved a decade ago by Ding, Sly and Sun~\cite{ding2015proof,ding2022proof} using the heavy machinery of the second moment method, the case of general $k$ eluded proof until ~\cite{GCarenini} and~\cite{k-sat-OpenAI}. In this short note we provide a ''human-friendly'' and detailed exposition of the OpenAI's resolution of the conjecture.

title: Scalable Spatio-Temporal SE(3) Diffusion for Long-Horizon Protein Dynamics
text:
Title: Scalable Spatio-Temporal SE(3) Diffusion for Long-Horizon Protein Dynamics
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations remain the gold standard for studying protein dynamics, but their computational cost limits access to biologically relevant timescales. Recent generative models have shown promise in accelerating simulations, yet they struggle with long-horizon generation due to architectural constraints, error accumulation, and inadequate modeling of spatio-temporal dynamics. We present STAR-MD (Spatio-Temporal Autoregressive Rollout for Molecular Dynamics), a scalable SE(3)-equivariant diffusion model that generates physically plausible protein trajectories over microsecond timescales. Our key innovation is a causal diffusion transformer with joint spatio-temporal attention that efficiently captures complex space-time dependencies while avoiding the memory bottlenecks of existing methods. On the standard ATLAS benchmark, STAR-MD achieves state-of-the-art performance across all metrics--substantially improving conformational coverage, structural validity, and dynamic fidelity compared to previous methods. STAR-MD successfully extrapolates to generate stable microsecond-scale trajectories where baseline methods fail catastrophically, maintaining high structural quality throughout the extended rollout. Our comprehensive evaluation reveals severe limitations in current models for long-horizon generation, while demonstrating that STAR-MD's joint spatio-temporal modeling enables robust dynamics simulation at biologically relevant timescales, paving the way for accelerated exploration of protein function.

title: Prospects for Near-Far Constraints on Reionization from Simulated LSST Observations of Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies and Stellar Streams
text:
Title: Prospects for Near-Far Constraints on Reionization from Simulated LSST Observations of Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies and Stellar Streams
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) will detect resolved stellar populations of intact dwarf galaxies and disrupted stellar streams in the Milky Way (MW) halo and beyond, opening a new avenue for near-field cosmology, particularly for constraining the faint galaxies during reionization. To interpret these data, we present and publicly release mock LSST catalogs of satellites, stellar streams, phase-mixed galaxies, and field galaxies around 13 MW-mass hosts in the FIRE-2 zoom-in simulations, generated with \textsf{py-ananke}. Using a surface brightness limit of $μ_{g} \leq 34$ $\rm{mag}$ $\rm{arcsec^{-2}}$, we find that $\approx29\%$ of streams with $M_{\star} \gtrsim 5 \times 10^5$ $M_{\odot}$ are detectable with tidal tails, while another $\approx38\%$ are detectable only through their bound progenitors and would appear as satellites. We estimate that $\approx96\%$ of satellites and $\approx64\%$ of field galaxies (out to $\sim$3.5 Mpc) with $M_{\star} \gtrsim 10^{5}$ $M_{\odot}$ are detectable, decreasing to $\approx$59\% and $\approx$42\% for $M_{\star} \gtrsim 10^{4.5}$ $M_{\odot}$ owing to resolution limits. Including streams detectable as satellites reproduces the radial distribution of observed MW satellites, suggesting that some observed satellites may be bound remnants of disrupted systems. Our mock galaxies match the sizes of observed satellites with $M_{\rm{V}} \lesssim -6$. Star-formation histories computed from only the detectable stars broadly recover the simulated star-formation histories. As an application, we test the near-far technique for reconstructing the proto-MW ultraviolet luminosity function (UVLF) during reionization ($z \gtrsim 6$). Adding the detectable streams improves the recovered faint-end slope at $z = 7$ and reduces the halo-to-halo scatter by $\approx33\%$.

title: Multivariate Bernstein duality for tournament Wright--Fisher diffusions
text:
Title: Multivariate Bernstein duality for tournament Wright--Fisher diffusions
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We give a probabilistic proof of a multivariate Bernstein duality for a multivariate Wright--Fisher frequency process with selection encoded by a finite tournament. The construction includes nontransitive interactions, such as rock--paper--scissors selection. Its dual is a pure-jump process of coefficient functions in the multinomial Bernstein basis. Selection increases the Bernstein degree through a winner--loser averaging operator, whereas neutral resampling decreases it through a duplication operator. For the proof, we construct a continuous forward process independently of duality, use duality to establish uniqueness, and obtain a weak stochastic differential equation representation and invariance of the simplex faces. This provides a sampling-based treatment of the tournament specialization of multitype Bernstein duality, extending an open problem in the binary Kingman setting of Cordero, Hummel, and Schertzer (2022).

title: Conformal boundaries and the photon sphere of AdS black holes
text:
Title: Conformal boundaries and the photon sphere of AdS black holes
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

We study linearized gravitational perturbations of four-dimensional Schwarzschild-AdS black holes with finite timelike boundaries subject to conformal boundary conditions. These fix the conformal class of the induced metric and the mean curvature, while allowing the boundary Weyl mode to fluctuate. The photon sphere plays a distinguished role in this problem: a static boundary at this radius is totally umbilic, and the scalar problem separates exactly into independent bulk and boundary sectors. We prove the absence of exponentially growing scalar and vector modes for spherical harmonics of degree two and higher. We determine how large angular momentum instabilities are suppressed as the boundary approaches umbilicity. Near the horizon, we recover the universal Rindler spectrum, including sound and shear excitations. We numerically follow these fluid modes as the boundary is moved outwards and find that they approach standard gravitational quasinormal modes at the asymptotic AdS$_4$ boundary. For large black holes, these asymptotic endpoints correspond to the sound and shear poles of the dual three-dimensional conformal field theory. We also study perturbations of the AdS$_4$ black brane, where we find an analogous continuation of the fluid modes in the absence of an intermediate umbilic boundary.

title: Identifiable but Hard to Estimate: Rotation in Equally Spaced Overcomplete ICA
text:
Title: Identifiable but Hard to Estimate: Rotation in Equally Spaced Overcomplete ICA
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

How many observations are needed to estimate a common rotation in two-dimensional overcomplete independent component analysis? We study equally spaced mixing columns with known source count, common source law, and column norm. For a fixed non-Gaussian fourth-order Gram-Charlier source law, the rotation is identifiable modulo the column spacing. Yet the sample size for fixed relative angular accuracy grows exponentially with the source count. We characterize this sample size, up to absolute constants, by the reciprocal of the squared Hellinger distance between two rotations separated by half the column spacing. An explicit radially weighted phase estimator attains this scale uniformly over the rotation family, using the observation radius to prevent cancellation in the mean of an angular harmonic. We also determine the exact exponential decay rate of single-observation total variation for the same pair. This gives bounds on the sample size exponent; its exact value remains open. Finally, a noisy binary-source example shows how an exact zero line of the observed characteristic function can have an exponentially small normal derivative.

title: Quantum oblique eigenprojection
text:
Title: Quantum oblique eigenprojection
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Every square matrix decomposes its underlying Hilbert space into generalized, nonorthogonal eigensubspaces. We show that a quantum computer can perform such an oblique eigenprojection $Π$ given block encoding access to the input matrix. Our approach has a query complexity nearly linear in the inverse gap and a normalization factor close to $\lVertΠ\rVert$ under a spectral-set condition on the input. This covers common assumptions on the numerical range or diagonalizability and matches known results for orthogonal eigenprojections. We achieve this with a two-sided block preconditioning that uses a discrete Fourier transform of the matrix resolvent. We describe applications to: (i) preparing eigenstates of matrices with complex eigenvalues, extending the quantum eigenvalue transformation algorithm of Low and Su beyond real spectra; (ii) solving continuous-time algebraic Riccati equations, cubically speeding up a prior solver of Rodenas-Ruiz, Zhao, and Lee; and (iii) solving ordinary Sylvester equations, quadratically improving a direct augmented method of Wang and Liu. Our result suggests a promising route to applying nonanalytic matrix functions on quantum computers.

title: Controlled Knowledge Engineering for Taxonomy Induction with Tool-Grounded LLM Agents and Runtime-Adaptive Policies
text:
Title: Controlled Knowledge Engineering for Taxonomy Induction with Tool-Grounded LLM Agents and Runtime-Adaptive Policies
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

Taxonomies are structured knowledge representations that support semantic search, recommendation, product catalog organization, and retrieval-augmented generation. Their automated construction from a fixed set of candidate entities requires more than plausible text generation: the resulting hierarchy must be complete, structurally valid, and semantically coherent. Large Language Models (LLMs) are promising for this task, but iterative free-form generation remains vulnerable to omitted or hallucinated entities, invalid hierarchical relations, and inconsistent organizational principles. We introduce TIGA (Taxonomy Induction with Tool-Grounded Agents), a knowledge-engineering architecture that formulates taxonomy induction as an iterative decision process over an explicit state and constrained action space. TIGA combines executable taxonomy-editing tools, an memory that records tool calls, rationales, and outcomes, and a runtime-adaptive organizational policy that the agent revises during inference. An optional global reviewer evaluates the constructed taxonomy against the candidate set and the active policy. We evaluate TIGA on four benchmark taxonomies using two LLM backbones and compare it with single-shot and iterative prompting-based baselines. TIGA achieves the strongest structural-quality results in most evaluated configurations, but does not dominate on every precision measure. The gains are accompanied by substantially higher token consumption, API-call volume, and inference time. Ablation results show consistent benefits from the policy and interaction-memory components, whereas the effect of global review depends on the dataset and the available revision budget. These findings characterize tool grounding and runtime policy adaptation as promising but costly mechanisms for improving the controlled construction of structured knowledge representations.

title: Dimensionally Regulated Graviton Self-Energy from Gravitons on de Sitter
text:
Title: Dimensionally Regulated Graviton Self-Energy from Gravitons on de Sitter
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

The graviton self-energy $-i [\mbox{}^{μν} Σ^{ρσ}](x;x')$ is the 1PI 2-point function of quantum gravity. It can be used to quantum-correct the linearized Einstein equation in order to infer quantum corrections to gravitational radiation and to the force of gravity. As long as the two points are non-coincident, the graviton self-energy does not need regularization at 1-loop order, however, solving the 1-loop effective field equations requires integrating $[\mbox{}^{μν} Σ^{ρσ}](x;x')$ over ${x'}^μ$, including ${x'}^μ = x^μ$. To facilitate this we employ dimensional regularization and BPHZ renormalization to compute the 1-loop contribution to the graviton self-energy, in pure quantum gravity, on de Sitter background, in the simplest gauge. We then solve the effective field equations to derive 1-loop corrections to the plane wave mode functions of gravitational radiation, and to the Newtonian potential. Although it seems possible to renormalize in such a way that the mode function shows no secular growth, the Newtonian potential grows like the third power of the number of e-foldings.

title: Development of a Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Transition State Search in Molecular Systems: A Transferable Model Across Structural and Dimensional Variations
text:
Title: Development of a Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Transition State Search in Molecular Systems: A Transferable Model Across Structural and Dimensional Variations
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

We developed a DRL approach for TS searches combining the deep Q-network and the bidirectional long short-term memory architectures to handle variable-sized molecular systems. We applied our method to 1,3,5-hexatriene (Triene), alanine dipeptide (Ala2), and 1,3,5,7-octatetraene (Tetraene) as target systems with the search space limited to backbone dihedral angles. Our model successfully learned the TS search tasks for all examined systems. More importantly, we demonstrate that our model pre-trained on Triene exhibits distinct transfer-learning capabilities across both backbone modifications (Triene to Ala2) and chain extensions (Triene to Tetraene). Such transferability is highly promising for future applications to molecules in general, as it allows an agent trained on simple systems to accelerate TS searches in larger or more complex ones. We expect that these findings on cross-system transferability represent an important step forward in developing DRL-based approaches for TS searches.

title: System Optimizations for Cost-Efficient Agent Harnesses
text:
Title: System Optimizations for Cost-Efficient Agent Harnesses
Domain: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

AI agent harnesses play the critical role of providing LLMs with an interface to a computing environment. Recent studies show that AI agents' task-execution accuracy depends mostly on the LLM used, while harness-side variances such as system prompts or tools have minimal impact. Rather, such harness-side variances show a larger impact on the cost of agent executions, achieving cost reductions up to 2.6 times on the same model and task. To further explore these harness-side cost optimization opportunities, we analyze the cost accumulation patterns across various agent traces and identify system opportunities to reduce token use and LLM calls without modifying the model or affecting task accuracy. Based on this analysis, we design Agency, a harness interposition platform that provides a unified abstraction and allows easy and portable implementation of harness-side system optimizations on existing off-the-shelf harnesses such as Claude Code or OpenAI Codex. Using Agency, we implement proof-of-concept optimization techniques based on our analysis and achieve cost reductions up to 35% across various real-world benchmarks on existing harnesses without compromising accuracy.

title: Emission line stacking on cosmological scales: equivalence to two-point statistics and modelling of the observational effects
text:
Title: Emission line stacking on cosmological scales: equivalence to two-point statistics and modelling of the observational effects
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Emission line stacking measurement for cosmological line intensity mapping (LIM) contains not only the average emission line profile of the stacked sources, but usually also the clustering signal, due to the limited angular resolution of the observations. We provide an explicit derivation of the equivalence between the emission line stacking, the two-point cross-correlation function in configuration space and the power spectrum in Fourier space, similar to the case between the angular stacking signal for the kinematic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect and the angular power spectrum in harmonic space (arXiv:2512.14625, arXiv:2605.15947). Using the quadratic estimator formalism, we establish that the emission line stacking signal measurement is equivalent to a quadratic estimator for the cross-correlation function. The formalism allows for the explicit modelling of the stacked signal, including the clustering statistics as well as observational effects such as the galaxy selection function and the LIM survey footprint. In particular, using mock HI intensity mapping data, we show that we can accurately model the effects of foreground removal on the stacked signal. The correlation function estimator provides significant speed-up for the stacking measurement and enables modelling of the signal and its covariance for large LIM datasets with MeerKLASS and future SKAO.

title: Magnetic-Field-Tuned Critical End Point and High-Field Phases in HoMn6Sn6
text:
Title: Magnetic-Field-Tuned Critical End Point and High-Field Phases in HoMn6Sn6
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Topological Kagome RMn6Sn6 materials, where R is a rare-earth, exhibit a rich variety of magnetic phases which provide an opportunity to understand how different spin textures affect topological and transport properties through the application of magnetic field H. In this work, we report experiments on single-crystal HoMn6Sn6, made possible by pulsed magnetic fields of up to 60 T, that permit high-field features of the field-temperature phase diagram to be studied in detail using magnetometry. Complementary, sensitive transport experiments over the same field range employ focused-ion-beam fabrication of novel strain-relieved HoMn6Sn6 devices. In agreement with meanfield calculations, we find a metamagnetic transition at 45 T with H||c between canted phases that ends in a critical end point at about 90 K. As far as we are aware, this is the only critical endpoint that is observed within the RMn6Sn6 kagome metals, and its temperature and field far exceed those of analogous phenomena in other materials. In the low-temperature metamagnetic region, HoMn6Sn6 shows large magnetoresistance, reaching 900 % at 60 T, in concert with Shubnikov de Haas oscillations that suggest a slight Fermi-surface contraction as the metamagnetic transition is crossed. A phase analysis of the oscillations suggests non-trivial band topology, although a firmer attribution must await detailed bandstructure calculations. Near the critical end point, we find deviations from Fermi-liquid behavior in the temperature-dependent magnetoresistance. In the metamagnetic region, the anomalous Hall contribution is not proportional to magnetization, and peaks at about 40 K, suggesting the role of enhanced spin fluctuations near the critical point. At higher temperatures, the anomalous Hall effect reappears at low fields, showing that the magnetization provided by the Ho and Mn sublattices independently affect the conductivity.

title: PFArena: Benchmarking Language Models for Protein Modification
text:
Title: PFArena: Benchmarking Language Models for Protein Modification
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Protein modification requires navigating an immense sequence space, yet wet-lab validation remains low-throughput and costly. Although computational paradigms including protein language models (PLMs), large language models (LLMs), and LLM-based agents have shown promise in protein modification, their relative efficacy across realistic experimental decision-making settings remains unclear. To bridge this gap, we introduce PFArena, a benchmark comprising four controlled task interfaces that cover single-mutant generation and multi-mutant ranking. By providing varying levels of mutation fitness data, PFArena reflects four representative research scenarios characterized by differing degrees of prior experimental context. We assess six PLMs, six LLMs, and five LLM-based agents using complementary metrics to measure both peak and overall protein modification performance. Our evaluation reveals that model performance shifts systematically with the availability of target-specific experimental evidence: PLMs demonstrate proficiency in open-ended single-mutant generation by leveraging protein-specific priors, whereas LLMs and agents perform strongly in multi-mutant ranking, particularly when target-specific fitness data are available. Nevertheless, all model families face fundamental challenges with increasing search-space size and mutation depth. We release our code and benchmark suite to facilitate reproducible research in model-assisted protein modification.

title: Direction-Selective Anomalous Quantum Transport from Saddle-like Topological Surface States Coupled to an Electronic Instability in YbSb$_{2}$
text:
Title: Direction-Selective Anomalous Quantum Transport from Saddle-like Topological Surface States Coupled to an Electronic Instability in YbSb$_{2}$
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

We report direction-selective anomalous quantum transport in epitaxial YbSb$_{2}$ thin films associated with an interplay between anisotropic topological surface states and an electronic instability. Quantum oscillations reveal a quasi-two-dimensional orbit with a non-trivial Berry phase and Dirac-like dispersion, observable for current along the $a$-axis but absent along the orthogonal in-plane $c$-axis. Together with first-principles calculations, these observations support its assignment to a saddle-like topological surface state. Its oscillation amplitude exhibits a field-dependent, non-monotonic temperature evolution that departs from conventional Lifshitz-Kosevich behavior. Raman and coherent phonon spectroscopy reveal additional low-temperature modes consistent with a density-wave instability. Their pronounced polarization anisotropy and colossal field-induced Raman enhancement suggest a strongly anisotropic, field-enhanced electronic susceptibility associated with the density-wave modes. Our findings point to dynamical coupling between anisotropic topological surface states and a field-responsive density-wave instability as a route to direction-selective anomalous quantum transport.

title: Observing mixed-state Uhlmann winding numbers in integrated photonic quantum walks
text:
Title: Observing mixed-state Uhlmann winding numbers in integrated photonic quantum walks
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Integer winding numbers provide a well-established classification of topological phases protected by chiral symmetry at zero temperature, but extending this classification to thermal mixed states remains challenging. The Uhlmann phase, a mixed-state extension of the Berry phase, provides a geometric framework for characterizing finite-temperature topology. However, this geometric phase is restricted to two quantized values and therefore cannot resolve the multiple thermal regimes associated with high winding numbers. Here, we experimentally observe integer mixed-state winding numbers in a photonic quantum-walk chip. We prepare and reconstruct thermal states associated with high-winding chiral Hamiltonians and their spectrum-preserving dimensional extensions. The reconstructed Uhlmann overlaps form closed trajectories in the complex plane, and their integer windings around the zero-overlap point are directly observed. As temperature increases, the Uhlmann winding number undergoes multiple discrete changes, accompanied by switches of the Uhlmann phase and the successive disappearance of momentum-resolved topological kinks. These results highlight an integer-valued topological characterization alongside the mixed-state geometric phase.

title: CrossScale-GLIO: Topology-Preserving Vision-Language Alignment of MRI and Whole-Slide Histopathology for Diffuse Glioma
text:
Title: CrossScale-GLIO: Topology-Preserving Vision-Language Alignment of MRI and Whole-Slide Histopathology for Diffuse Glioma
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Magnetic resonance imaging and histopathology observe the same glioma at radically different scales. We present CrossScale-GLIO, a visual multimodal framework that represents MRI as a tumor-habitat graph and histology as a cell-niche graph, then aligns them with a structure-aware optimal transport objective anchored by diagnostic language. Across paired and external glioma cohorts, CrossScale-GLIO achieved a paired-test subtype macro-F1 of 0.789, IDH AUROC of 0.934, 1p/19q AUROC of 0.884, and MGMT AUROC of 0.802. The subtype gain over feature-only transport was 2.8 percentage points (95% CI: 1.2 to 4.4, adjusted p = 0.0019). Bidirectional patient retrieval reached Recall@1 values of 0.286 and 0.278, and Recall@5 values of 0.621 and 0.608. Pathologists rated 81.2% of high-mass habitat-niche pairs as biologically plausible. Deleting the highest-mass pair reduced correct-class probability by 0.184, compared with 0.049 under random deletion. Degree-preserving graph rewiring reduced subtype macro-F1 by 0.034 and retrieval Recall@1 by 0.090, directly confirming that preserved relational topology drives cross-scale correspondence.

title: Deep Learning GW Quasiparticle Hamiltonians for Many-Body Excited-State Electronic Structure at Scale
text:
Title: Deep Learning GW Quasiparticle Hamiltonians for Many-Body Excited-State Electronic Structure at Scale
Domain: Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph)

Accurate quasiparticle electronic structures are the foundation for understanding excited-state properties of materials and explaining optoelectronic, quantum, and transport phenomena. First-principles GW calculations nevertheless remain computationally intensive for large or configurationally complex systems. Here we introduce DeepH-GW, a deep-learning framework that predicts an effective GW quasiparticle Hamiltonian directly from atomic structure. Building on the local, equivariant message-passing architecture of DeepH, DeepH-GW is trained on high-fidelity plane-wave GW calculations through a real-space Hamiltonian-reconstruction interface. This approach combines the systematic accuracy and broad chemical applicability of plane-wave methods with linear-scaling neural-network inference. Across the systems examined, DeepH-GW reproduces quasiparticle band structures with errors on the order of a few meV. Moreover, we show that, despite the intrinsic nonlocality of many-body interactions, DeepH-GW exhibits strong cross-scale transferability from relatively small training structures to substantially larger supercells. We demonstrate that the framework can accurately capture GW-level electron-phonon band-gap renormalization through predictions in supercells with thermal displacements, illustrating the power of the approach. DeepH-GW therefore provides a practical route toward large-scale many-body simulations and foundation models for excited-state electronic structure.

title: Reduction of the integro-differential equation to an ordinary differential equation in ruin models with investment in a risky asset
text:
Title: Reduction of the integro-differential equation to an ordinary differential equation in ruin models with investment in a risky asset
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We study ruin models with the surplus invested in a risky asset and Erlang-distributed claims: non-life insurance, annuity payments and the mixed model. Assuming that the integro-differential equation for the survival probability has a classical twice continuously differentiable solution, we prove that this solution satisfies a linear ordinary differential equation. We construct explicit annihilating operators and write the coefficients of the reduced equation in closed form through binomial coefficients (for the mixed model with equal shape parameters). A converse criterion is obtained: a bounded solution of the reduced equation satisfies the integro-differential equation if and only if the residual vanishes at zero initial capital together with its derivatives of order below that of the annihilator. The exponent of the power branch at infinity is determined by the parameters of the risky asset alone and does not depend on the shape parameter. For the mixed model we classify the fundamental set of solutions: the exponentially growing modes are excluded by boundedness. The connection coefficient of the power branch is nonzero by a known power-law lower bound for the ruin probability, and in the annuity model by the reduced equation and the boundary condition at zero. Hence the ruin probability has power-law asymptotics with a positive constant for all shape parameters and all positive exponents, and a complete asymptotic expansion up to a multiplicative constant in all three models. For non-life insurance with Erlang claims of order two the expansion coefficients are computed by an explicit recurrence.

title: Agentic AI-assisted coding offers a unique opportunity to instill epistemic grounding during software development
text:
Title: Agentic AI-assisted coding offers a unique opportunity to instill epistemic grounding during software development
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

The capabilities of AI-assisted coding are progressing at breakneck speed. Chat-based vibe coding has evolved into fully fledged AI-assisted, agentic software development using agent scaffolds where the human developer creates a plan that agentic AIs implement. One current trend is utilizing documents beyond this plan document, such as project and method-scoped documents. Here we propose GROUNDING$.$md, a community-governed, field-scoped epistemic grounding document, using mass spectrometry-based proteomics as an example. We have drafted a file specific to proteomics: proteomics_GROUNDING$.$md (available at https://github.com/OmicsGrounding/proteomics-grounding) to demonstrate what a GROUNDING$.$md would look like. This explicit field-scoped grounding document encodes Hard Constraints (non-negotiable validity invariants empirically required for scientific correctness) and Convention Parameters (community-agreed defaults) that override all other contexts to enforce validity, regardless of what the user prompts. In practice, this will empower a non-domain expert to generate code, tools, and software that have best practices baked in at the ground level, providing confidence to the software developer but also to those reviewing or using the final product. Undoubtedly it is easier to have agentic AIs adhere to guidelines than humans, and this opportunity allows for organizations to develop epistemic grounding documents in such a way as to keep domain experts in the loop in a future of democratized generation of bespoke software solutions.

title: Confidence Is Not a Promise: A Reference Audit of Typed Decision Models
text:
Title: Confidence Is Not a Promise: A Reference Audit of Typed Decision Models
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Typed decision models return a probability distribution over options supplied by the caller, and software tends to act on that number as if it were a guarantee. We measure what it licenses, comparing the open-weight Laya, in five checkpoints, with Jev 1.13, available only through an API. A probability licenses a statement about groups of decisions, not about one decision, and a gate that promises an accuracy among the cases it decides alone keeps that promise only with a lower bound checked on data like its traffic. Across 190 exchangeable evaluations, a threshold chosen by point estimate breaks the promise in 147, Learn then Test keeps it in all of them, and a Beta lower-bound rule decides more items on average than Learn then Test in 128 and fewer in none, without its guarantee. Calibrated in English, Jev keeps a promise of 95% in 8 of 51 locales. Ordinary typing noise breaks a promise calibrated on clean text, and, in exploratory runs, training with noise raises the noisy accuracy with no loss on clean text. In four further domains, a fine-tuned Laya needs from 250 to 8,000 labels to be non-inferior to Jev, and does not get there on LIAR2. Under drift, the preregistered claim for a Bayesian retraining loop is not supported: the loop avoids needless retraining where the change does not degrade the model, at a cost equivalent to recalibration alone, and re-qualifying the threshold in every window keeps the promise more often where it does. On the monthly series of M3, neither decider predicts the direction of the next value better than a constant answer. Confidence separates right from wrong answers with an AUROC from 0.80 to 0.96, but it does not select faithful explanations, and exact coalition games of single decisions show what an explanation can still say through an API that rounds to two decimals. We release the frozen answers with a datasheet, a promise check and the code.

title: Black-hole ringdown at an exceptional point
text:
Title: Black-hole ringdown at an exceptional point
Domain: High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

Black holes ring in damped oscillations. At an exceptional point, photon-sphere and near-horizon modes merge, and their response can acquire a linear time factor. We compute its amplitude from constrained Einstein-Maxwell data for a rotating, charged black hole in de Sitter space. With seven competing modes fixed, the late-time curvature error is 0.00383$\%$ for the pair and 0.01401$\%$ for a refitted exponential. We suppress the linear term by tuning the initial disturbance at fixed geometry. Hence, near coalescence, changing only the initial disturbance can shift the frequency inferred from a short ringdown fit.

title: Enforcing Axioms for AI Alignment under Loss-Based Rules
text:
Title: Enforcing Axioms for AI Alignment under Loss-Based Rules
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Many alignment methods, most notably reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), train reward models by minimizing a loss on pairwise comparisons of model responses. Inspired by principle-guided methods such as Constitutional AI, we treat each principle as a voter that compares responses according to that principle, for example, preferring the more helpful or less toxic response. We represent these voters as linear directions in a fixed embedding space, a simplifying assumption motivated by the Linear Representation Hypothesis. In this linear social choice model, Ge et al. (2024) showed that an optimal linear reward model can violate Pareto optimality (PO): From the principles-as-voters lens, this means a response A can be less helpful and more toxic than B, yet still receive a higher reward. We ask whether richer reward models or changes to comparison data can recover PO within loss-based training. We show that PO can still fail for polynomials of any fixed degree and one-hidden-layer ReLU multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) of any fixed width $ d\ge 2 $ with suitable finite parameter bounds. We then recover PO for loss-based training of linear rewards under suitable assumptions in an idealized setting with uniform comparison directions and equal comparison lengths. These results motivate dataset design as an approach to recovering PO in constitutional-style alignment while retaining loss-based training.

title: CRUSTPairs: A Cross-Language Dataset of Paired C and Rust Solutions
text:
Title: CRUSTPairs: A Cross-Language Dataset of Paired C and Rust Solutions
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

C-to-Rust migration is an active agenda, but no dataset pairs the two languages at the level of whole solutions to a shared problem. We present CRUSTPairs, 1857 C/Rust implementation pairs drawn from competitive programming archives, normalised, deduplicated, and stratified into difficulty tiers by zero-shot cross-language embedding similarity, with perrecord provenance and licensing. Cross-language retrieval is hard on this data, and harder than a single baseline would suggest: TF-IDF over shared identifiers reaches MRR 0.21 and so beats a pretrained code model at 0.19, which on the hardest quarter of the data scores 1.7x chance. Finetuning reaches 0.79, and lifts that hardest quarter 10x. Renaming every user identifier settles what is being learned: the finetuned models keep 96-97% of their accuracy without them, while the pretrained model keeps 66\% - less than the lexical baseline does - and on structurally divergent pairs the finetuned models are better without identifiers than with them.

title: Experimental demonstration of dual-polarization nonreciprocal thermal emission at moderate magnetic fields
text:
Title: Experimental demonstration of dual-polarization nonreciprocal thermal emission at moderate magnetic fields
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Conventional thermal emitters obey Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which requires emissivity and absorptivity to be equal at each wavelength, angle, and polarization. This in turn places a fundamental limit on a range of radiative energy technologies as well as heat transfer. This constraint can however be overcome using magneto-optic semiconductors, which break Lorentz reciprocity under an applied magnetic field. However, in most prior experimental demonstrations, nonreciprocity has been restricted to TM polarization, since the electric field of TE-polarized light is parallel to the applied magnetic field. Here, we experimentally demonstrate nonreciprocal absorption in both polarizations at the same wavelengths and angles from a single structure, wherein a germanium Mie-resonant metasurface on a doped InAs layer scatters TE-polarized light into near fields with components perpendicular to the magnetic field, allowing the magneto-optic response of the InAs to act on them. Under a 0.48 T field from a permanent Halbach array, this structure exhibits a difference in absorptivity between $+B$ and $-B$ of 0.035 in both TE and TM polarization at 16.6 $μ$m. Our approach shows that the magneto-optic response of a planar semiconductor and the resonances of a dielectric metasurface can be designed together, offering a potential route to dual-polarization nonreciprocity at fields available from permanent magnets for emerging energy and heat transfer technologies.

title: Quantum-enabled measurement of gravitational forces at the milligram scale
text:
Title: Quantum-enabled measurement of gravitational forces at the milligram scale
Domain: Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

Gravity is by far the weakest among all known interactions. While it dominates the large-scale structure of the universe, gravitational interactions between small masses in the microscopic range remain underexplored because they are too weak to be experimentally accessible. The interface between gravity, described by general relativity, and quantum mechanics, which describes the microscopic world, is of particular interest. From a theory standpoint, these two major descriptions of nature have not been combined in a satisfactory manner. Technology is gradually becoming mature enough such that probing gravity at the microscopic scale, where quantum mechanics and gravity potentially meet, is becoming accessible. Explorations towards genuine quantum gravity have to be carried out under conditions where the gravitating masses possess non-classical properties, which necessitates ultimate protection against disturbances, such as ultralow temperatures and a small range of motion. Here, we present an experiment at millikelvin temperatures, where the gravity due to a micron-range coherent displacement of an 87 mg source mass imprints on the motion of an oscillating membrane loaded with a 1.3 mg test mass. Vibrations of the membrane are measured in the microwave optomechanical scheme, which is a key setup for investigating non-classical motional states of mechanical oscillators. When considering the combination of total source and test masses, our setup presents two orders of magnitude progress in sensing gravity at the small scale, as well as a 35 dB improvement of gravitational sensitivity at kHz frequencies or above. Our setup offers a plausible approach for studying gravitational interactions between masses prepared in non-classical motional states.

title: Peptide Structure Prediction Using Counter-Diabatic Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (CD-QAOA)
text:
Title: Peptide Structure Prediction Using Counter-Diabatic Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (CD-QAOA)
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

In this study, we predicted the structure of the heptapeptide APRLRFY, a neuropeptide sequence, on a tetrahedral lattice using a Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). QAOA is based on the adiabatic approximation and has been successfully applied to a wide range of optimization problems. However, relatively slow convergence during ground-state searches has frequently been reported. To overcome this limitation, we employed the Counter-Diabatic Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (CD-QAOA), which introduces an additional counter-diabatic driving term into the adiabatic framework to accelerate convergence toward the ground state during peptide structure prediction. In the heptapeptide structure prediction, intermolecular interactions were modeled using two different approaches. In the first approach, only the interaction between the second residue, proline (P), and the seventh residue, tyrosine (Y), was included in the optimization. In the second approach, all residue-residue interactions within the heptapeptide were modeled using the Miyazawa-Jernigan (MJ) interaction matrix. To validate the peptide structures predicted using CD-QAOA, we additionally employed several classical computational methods, including quantum chemistry-based Hartree-Fock (HF) calculation and Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculation, conventional molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and Hamiltonian replica exchange molecular dynamics (H-REMD) simulation. The structural similarities among the conformations obtained from these different approaches were systematically analyzed. CD-QAOA is highly effective for predicting the structures of short peptides. In particular, we demonstrate that a quantum-classical hybrid framework can significantly improve both the efficiency and accuracy of peptide structure prediction.

title: One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge
text:
Title: One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

We describe our solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge: 100 long-horizon household tasks in the OmniGibson simulator. We placed 9th on the final leaderboard, the only independent team in the top 10. The core of the solution is a single vision-language-action (VLA) model, one checkpoint for all 100 tasks, built on our 1st-place 2025 solution, which is based on $π_{0.5}$. On the 50 tasks shared with 2025, its Q rises from 0.260 to 0.371; across all 100 tasks it scores 0.392. Our main conclusion from 2025 was that the model was undertrained, so most of the 2026 work went into training the model for longer, optimizing some training parameters, making each training step slightly faster and reducing the gradient noise: a migration from 50 to 100 tasks (semantic stages built from the demonstrations' skill annotations, task and stage embeddings of new tasks warm-started from similar old ones, and a 21-dimensional action space matching the teleoperation controls); variance-reduced multi-sample flow matching with a simple noise-vs-compute model that picks the number of action-expert samples per observation without ablations; and a 200k-step training run, about one pass over the 211M frames of the demonstrations. A cloud evaluation infrastructure keeps a shared record with provenance, episode diagnostics and restorable simulator states, and runs six simulators on one GPU together faster than real time. On top of the learned policy, 14 tasks are routed to a GPT-6 Astra coding agent that controls the robot through observation and motion tools, starting every episode from a frozen copy of its own practice session on training instances. Across these 14 tasks, Astra's mean Q is 0.639, against 0.108 for the learned policy. The public submission included only part of the Astra results and scored 0.446 Q with 27.3% full-task success.

title: AlloGen: Conformation-Selective Binder Generation with Differential State Scoring
text:
Title: AlloGen: Conformation-Selective Binder Generation with Differential State Scoring
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Protein binder design has largely optimized for affinity alone, leaving conformational selectivity unaddressed: for allosteric targets such as kinases, nuclear receptors, and GPCRs, a binder that engages both active and inactive states provides no functional specificity regardless of how tightly it binds. We introduce AlloGen, a modular framework that decouples backbone generation from a learned state-selectivity scorer $Q_θ$, an SE(3)-invariant interface graph transformer trained via a two-phase curriculum that first learns interface geometry before imposing conformational discrimination. Because $Q_θ$ is fully differentiable and generator-agnostic, it integrates with any backbone generator as a passive reranker or an active gradient-based guide without retraining. Across a diverse benchmark of proteins spanning multiple families and conformational mechanisms, AlloGen consistently identifies binders that preferentially recognize desired structural states while rejecting alternative conformations. Experimental validation on calmodulin further demonstrates that these computational selectivity signals translate to physical molecules, yielding de novo peptides that bind the desired holo conformation while exhibiting no detectable binding to the apo state. Together, these results establish conformational selectivity as a learnable property and provide a general framework for state-selective protein binder design.

title: Unprompted coordination through shared memory in LLM agents: a locked two-implementation replication and extension
text:
Title: Unprompted coordination through shared memory in LLM agents: a locked two-implementation replication and extension
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Coordination between large language-model agents has become a central question for AI safety and software engineering, as such agents are deployed in groups that share infrastructure. Existing research tells the agents that partners exist or asks them to coordinate. Whether coordination arises through shared state alone, with nothing disclosing that anyone else is present, is the key question for deployments that share caches and memory between agents, yet it has rarely been examined, and never with independent replication; this study does both. Four agents each received a short arithmetic task and a key-value store presented to each as its own scratch space; two held complementary halves of one computation, and no prompt mentioned other agents, sharing or collaboration. For reliability, the environment was rebuilt independently from a written protocol, and both implementations ran under hashed locks on design, data and analysis. The results bear novelty value in three respects. Joint success occurred only through the shared store. Whether a model coordinated depended not on its vendor tier but on whether it wrote its intermediate result and looked at the store again, and one ordinary sentence, "check your workspace again before submitting", switched that second look on and off. The findings held under replication. For practice, state shared between agents is a communication channel and should be separated, namespaced and logged. For research, designs should be locked before the data, and the parse rule, endpoint and parameters reported. Future work should test open-weight models and separate using another agent's output from intending to communicate.

title: Backward--forward interacting systems with probability-valued strategies and common noise
text:
Title: Backward--forward interacting systems with probability-valued strategies and common noise
Domain: Probability (math.PR)

We study a system of interacting agents in which a backward stochastic equation is coupled to the forward evolution of a probability-valued strategy distribution. The agents interact through their empirical state--strategy law and are exposed to a common Brownian noise. Under Lipschitz, mass-conservation, and positivity assumptions, we establish well-posedness of the finite-agent system on a sufficiently short time interval. We then identify its large-population limit as a conditional mean-field backward--forward system and prove conditional propagation of chaos. When agent characteristics take finitely many values, we obtain order $N^{-1}$ bounds for the expected squared particle--copy error and the expected squared Wasserstein distance of order one between the empirical law and the conditional limiting law. An adaptive-strategy model with replicator dynamics illustrates the theory, accompanied by a numerical comparison of the two errors.

title: Observable-Reduction-Guided Sparse Regression for Partially Observed Active-Quiescent Systems
text:
Title: Observable-Reduction-Guided Sparse Regression for Partially Observed Active-Quiescent Systems
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Active-quiescent switching occurs in biological populations in which growth is confined to a proliferative active state, while cells may reversibly enter a nonproliferative quiescent state. Experiments often observe only part of this process, through active-state markers, aggregate population measurements, or aggregate data supplemented by sparse active-state observations. Such measurements arise when marker panels are limited, active-state assays require fixation or endpoint sampling, or only total cell number, optical density, tumor burden, or aggregate fluorescence is reported. These observation choices complicate sparse regression methods such as sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy), because the measured variable may satisfy a different equation from the underlying active-quiescent system. A library chosen for the wrong observable may therefore fit a trajectory without preserving mechanistic interpretation or transferability. We study this issue using a two-compartment ordinary differential equation model. We define observable reduction as the elimination of hidden states to obtain the differential equation satisfied by the measured variable. For several biologically relevant growth laws, we derive observation-specific reductions and use them to construct sparse-regression libraries. Using synthetic data, we compare these structured libraries with standard polynomial SINDy. Polynomial libraries can match training trajectories while failing coefficient-relation and transfer tests, whereas reduction-guided libraries recover interpretable coefficient maps when the observed regime is informative. These results show that interpretable equation learning in hidden-compartment systems requires matching both the regression target and candidate library to the observation process.

title: A Multi-Word Tokenizer for 204 Languages That Needs Fewer Tokens Than GPT-4o's, Including on English
text:
Title: A Multi-Word Tokenizer for 204 Languages That Needs Fewer Tokens Than GPT-4o's, Including on English
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Languages of India need 1.6 to 14 times as many tokens as English on GPT-4o's tokenizer for the same content, which makes them more expensive and slower to serve. We train tokenizers from scratch on human-written text in about 200 languages. Havon v3 is a byte-level BPE tokenizer with 262,144 tokens and a pre-tokenizer that keeps combining marks with their letters and chunks scripts written without spaces. On FLORES-200 devtest it needs fewer tokens than GPT-4o's o200k_base on all 25 languages of India (median 0.74 of GPT-4o's count) and on 172 of 204 languages, but 7% more on English. Havon v4 adds a second, multi-word training stage (SuperBPE) to v3. At exactly GPT-4o's vocabulary size of 200,019 tokens, v4 needs 6.1% fewer tokens than GPT-4o on English and fewer on 161 of 204 languages and all 25 languages of India (median 0.74); at the same size, v3 needs 9.4% more on English and wins on 133. With 262,144 tokens, v4 needs 9.6% fewer tokens on English and fewer on 182 of 204 languages, and with 524,288 tokens it needs fewer on 203 of 204. The gains are largest for English, Hindi and the Romance languages; scripts without spaces, such as Khmer, Burmese and Tibetan, gain little and lose subword merges. Havon v5 replaces v4's Python-only code sample with permissively licensed code in 15 languages: on code it needs 1.03 to 1.22 times GPT-4o's tokens, against 1.11 to 1.29 for v4, while keeping all 25 languages of India (median 0.74, all significant under a sentence-level bootstrap) and English (0.94). These are compression results only: we have not yet evaluated a model trained with v4 or v5.

title: PathXAI: Evidence-guided structured pathology reporting by transferable tissue segmentation
text:
Title: PathXAI: Evidence-guided structured pathology reporting by transferable tissue segmentation
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Pathology reporting translates tissue observations across regions and slides into diagnoses and supporting morphological descriptions, yet explicit tissue-composition measurements are rarely used to guide H&E-based report generation. We developed PathXAI, which pairs transferable tissue segmentation with a pretrained vision-language model. Because supplying tissue information directly with H&E images gave limited benefit, PathXAI-Report uses segmentation overlays and tissue statistics in separate steps, selects between candidate diagnoses by fixed rules, acquires further images when evidence is insufficient and records every step for review, without updating model weights. Its segmentation component exceeded baselines in mean Dice on internal and external tests. In automated evaluation on 1,200 public and 151 private cases, PathXAI achieved higher agreement with reference diagnoses and documented morphology than H&E-based comparators. On the public cohort, it exceeded Qwen+H&E by 4.4 percentage points in cancer family match rate and 5.7 percentage points in finding F1.

title: Beyond Point Photo-$z$ Estimates: Normalizing Flows for Tomographic $N(z)$ Reconstruction with DESI DR1
text:
Title: Beyond Point Photo-$z$ Estimates: Normalizing Flows for Tomographic $N(z)$ Reconstruction with DESI DR1
Domain: Cosmology and Extragalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)

Accurate calibration of tomographic redshift distributions, $N(z)$ is essential for cosmological analysis of weak lensing data. We investigate conditional normalizing flows (NFs) and compare their performance with random forest (RF) and quantile random forest (QRF) models. We consider DESI galaxy and quasar targets from DESI DR1 spectroscopic data and with the photometry from Legacy Surveys DR10. We train on 1.1 million sources and test on 2.0 million sources in a non-overlapping sky region ($0 1.6$. By introducing distribution-level metrics like Wasserstein distance and JS divergence, we find that stacking NF posterior PDFs provides more accurate tomographic $N(z)$ reconstruction than QRF, particularly at high redshifts. For $z_{\rm median}>2.5$, the NF achieves a smaller absolute mean-redshift bias ($0.060\pm0.031$ versus $0.318$) and higher probability overlap ($0.905\pm0.008$ versus $0.787$) than QRF. We apply redshift-dependent post-hoc PDF calibration derived from a held-out validation sample. After calibration, the absolute mean-redshift biases in four bins spanning $0.2<z_{\rm median}<1.0$ range from $0.0016$ to $0.0019$, with central values below referring benchmark $0.002(1+z)$. In the highest-redshift bin, calibration further reduces the bias to $0.016\pm0.011$. Our results demonstrate the potential of NF PDFs for tomographic $N(z)$ reconstruction while highlighting challenges in transferring models across galaxy populations.

title: Anisotropic Trust Region Warping for Prior-Data Fitted Networks in Bayesian Optimisation
text:
Title: Anisotropic Trust Region Warping for Prior-Data Fitted Networks in Bayesian Optimisation
Domain: Statistical Machine Learning (stat.ML)

Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs) replace the hyperparameter refitting of Gaussian Process (GP) surrogates in Bayesian optimisation with a single forward pass, at the cost of a prior that is fixed at meta-training time. We show empirically that a PFN's predictive log-likelihood falls increasingly behind that of a refitted GP as the objective function's lengthscale grows beyond the mode of the PFN's meta-training prior, and that this deficit carries over to optimisation performance. To correct the mismatch without retraining the network, we introduce Anisotropic Trust Region (ATR) warping. Per-dimension lengthscales are estimated by kernel target alignment, and an affine rescaling of the input space maps the objective onto the lengthscale the PFN expects, with a trust region around the anchor determining which observations are retained, leaving the PFN's $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot N^2)$ inference cost unchanged. On functions drawn from a Matérn-3/2 kernel, ATR warping improves optimisation performance of the PFN at both extremes of the lengthscale range. Our implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/youngers2006/Trust-Region-Warping-For-PFNs.

title: A Topology-Based Approach to Representative Volume Element Assessment in Solid Oxide Cell Anodes Using Large Volume Tomography and Persistent Homology
text:
Title: A Topology-Based Approach to Representative Volume Element Assessment in Solid Oxide Cell Anodes Using Large Volume Tomography and Persistent Homology
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Determining the representative volume element is essential for establishing statistically meaningful microstructure-property relationships. Conventional approaches rely on the convergence of selected geometric descriptors, which may yield different estimates of the representative volume. Here, we propose a topology-based framework for assessing the representative scale of a nickel-yttria-stabilized zirconia solid oxide cell anode reconstructed using plasma focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (121.8 um x 83.97 um x 45.99 um). Persistent homology was used to characterize the pore network, and normalized persistence images of subvolumes were compared with those of the largest available reference volume using the L1 distance. This provides a continuous measure of topological similarity across observation scales, rather than defining representativeness through a single convergence threshold. The topological distance decreases with increasing volume and is described by empirical exponential models over the investigated range (R2 in [0.972, 0.983]). Comparison with porosity and specific surface area highlights differences in the scale-dependent behavior of geometric and topological descriptors. The framework was also tested on three independent synthetic realizations, demonstrating its potential for quantitative assessment of topological similarity in porous microstructures.

title: Robust Flow Matching under Target Corruption and Label Noise
text:
Title: Robust Flow Matching under Target Corruption and Label Noise
Domain: Machine Learning (cs.LG)

Flow Matching (FM) is a strong framework for generative modeling due to its stable training and efficient sampling. However, FM assumes clean target data and labels, an assumption often violated in practice. We formulate FM training as a time-dependent regression problem over conditional vector fields and analyze how the two corruption types affect the objective: i) target corruption adds a time-dependent residual term that grows with time, ii) label noise causes updates to the wrong class-conditional vector field. Based on this analysis, we propose to improve FM robustness by mapping corruption-specific residual scores to sample weights. For target corruption, we propose the Temporal Residual Score (TRS), which emphasizes residual magnitudes at intermediate-to-late FM times, where clean and corrupted samples are more separable. For label noise, we propose the Comparative Conditional Score (CCS), which compares the residual of the observed class-conditional vector field against alternative class-conditional vector fields for the same trajectory and velocity target. Experiments across controlled corruption settings and real-world noisy labels show that the proposed methods improve robustness over standard FM and robust-training baselines, supporting corruption-specific residual structure as a practical basis for robust FM.

title: Folding, Reasoning, and Scaling with Open-source Drug Discovery Engine
text:
Title: Folding, Reasoning, and Scaling with Open-source Drug Discovery Engine
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Accurately modeling biomolecular interactions is a central bottleneck in biology and therapeutic discovery. Here, we introduce Open Drug Discovery Engine (OpenDDE), an open-source, all-atom biomolecular foundation model that uses co-folding as the entry point to a scalable AI-driven drug discovery engine. Rather than treating structure prediction as an isolated endpoint, OpenDDE is designed as a shared structural reasoning layer for modeling sequence-structure-function relationships across biomolecular complexes, enabling complex structure prediction today while providing a foundation for de novo design, affinity estimation, structure-conditioned optimization, and more. OpenDDE integrates advances in all-atom architecture, atomic latent reasoning, inference optimization, and large-scale data processing to achieve IsoDDE-level co-folding accuracy within a reproducible and openly accessible framework. We also identify two scaling-law directions for co-folding models, revealing practical routes for continued improvement through data, model, inference, and training scaling. By releasing training code, inference pipelines, checkpoints, and benchmarks, OpenDDE aims to democratize access to frontier biomolecular intelligence, accelerate global collaboration, and lay an open foundation for next-generation drug discovery systems that can move from predicting molecular structures toward designing, scoring, and optimizing therapeutic candidates for human health.

title: Cubic-Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te optical modes across the phonon and phonon-polariton regimes
text:
Title: Cubic-Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te optical modes across the phonon and phonon-polariton regimes
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Alloying offers a convenient route to tune the physical properties of semiconductors, at the price, however, of local lattice/bond distortions needed to accommodate the lattice mismatch. Being nearly lattice-matched and moreover highly resistant to lattice and bond distortions thanks to a largely covalent bonding, cubic Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te sets a benchmark to test the sensitivity of lattice vibrations to minimum lattice and bond distortions induced by alloying. We explore experimentally the two transverse optical regimes of cubic Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te (x<0.7), with ab initio calculations in support: (1) the phonon-polariton regime at quasi-infinite (photon-like) wavelengths averaging over the alloy disorder, probed by forward-Raman scattering, and (2) the purely-mechanical phonon regime down to minimum wavelengths nearly matching the lattice constant zooming into the alloy disorder, achieved by inelastic neutron scattering. The short Zn-Te bond is found to exhibit a compact optical duo distinguishing homo from hetero local bond environments (1 bond: 2 mode), as explained by the percolation model. This deviates from the historical Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te MREI (modified-random-element-isodisplacement) scheme inspired from classical Raman and infrared studies, in which the optical modes are blind to the bond environment (1-bond: 1-mode). So, the test is positive, reinforcing the status of the percolation scheme as a robust decryptor of (even small) lattice distortions induced by alloying through the lattice dynamics.

title: zkARc: Succinctly Verifiable Proofs for Neurosymbolic Natural Language Formalization and Verification
text:
Title: zkARc: Succinctly Verifiable Proofs for Neurosymbolic Natural Language Formalization and Verification
Domain: Computation and Language (cs.CL)

Autonomous agents increasingly execute consequential actions on behalf of users, but ordinary middleware guardrails do not provide cryptographic proof that a policy was actually enforced. Their verdicts leave counterparties dependent on the operator unless they repeat the checks themselves, potentially exposing sensitive policies and inputs. We present zkARc, a modular proof-carrying framework that wraps each stage of Automated Reasoning checks (ARc) in an independent, succinctly verifiable zero-knowledge proof. ARc is a neurosymbolic system that translates natural language policies into formal logic and verifies AI-generated content against them using SMT solvers. zkARc certifies the planner's output, the policy's formalization, the action's formalization and both solver queries. The receipt binds these computations to the exact action received and, under the stated assumptions, reveals no additional information about private policies and intermediate model values beyond the declared public information and verdict. This lets a third party check the claimed policy enforcement without re-running the pipeline or trusting the operator. We prove completeness, knowledge soundness and zero knowledge for the composed receipt under explicit assumptions. An implementation on Qwen2-0.5B enforces a spending policy end to end, approving two purchases and denying a third. A full receipt, which also proves model inference, takes about an hour to issue with CPU-only proving and verifies in under a minute, and the solver proof alone is 88 KiB and verifies in 0.3 seconds.

title: Network Characteristics of Individual Pigments in Cyanobacterial Photosystem II Core Complexes
text:
Title: Network Characteristics of Individual Pigments in Cyanobacterial Photosystem II Core Complexes
Domain: Biomolecules (q-bio.BM)

Part of the excitation energy transfer (EET) characteristics of the photosystem II (PSII) comes from the interconnection between pigments. To understand the correlation between the EET and the pigments' interaction structure, we construct a network from the EET rates, which are related to both the distance between the pigments (chlorophylls and pheophytins) and their spatial orientations. Especially, we investigate how well the PS II core complex's EET functionality can be explained by using only the network topology in Thermosynechococcus vulcanus 1.9 Å. Starting from the Förster theory, we construct a network of EET pathways. For an analysis of the network structure, we calculate common network-structural measures like betweenness centrality, eigenvector centrality and weighted clustering. These measures can reflect the role of individual pigments in the EET network. In our work, we found that some well-known properties were reproduced by the network analysis of the simplified network, which means that the topology of the network encodes functionally relevant information. For example, from the network structural analysis, we can infer that most of the chlorophyll molecules (chlorophylls) in the pigment-protein complex CP47 have a heightened probability of transferring energy compared with other chlorophylls. We also see that the active branch chlorophylls in the reaction center are characterized by a high eigenvector centrality, a high betweenness centrality, and a low weighted clustering coefficient. This is indicative of functionally important vertices.

title: An Electrolyte Equation of State Based on openCOSMO-RS: From Aqueous Solutions to Non-Aqueous Systems
text:
Title: An Electrolyte Equation of State Based on openCOSMO-RS: From Aqueous Solutions to Non-Aqueous Systems
Domain: Chemical Physics (physics.chem-ph)

Predictive COSMO-RS-based electrolyte models such as COSMO-RS-ES describe electrolyte solutions from quantum-chemical information, but treat the liquid as incompressible and give no access to densities or pressure effects. This work presents openCOSMO-RS-ES-Phi, to our knowledge the first open-source implementation of a predictive electrolyte equation of state based on openCOSMO-RS. It combines the COSMO-RS-based equation of state openCOSMO-RS-Phi with the ion interaction energies and the long-range term of COSMO-RS-ES, which is first refitted on the same simplified short range. With this refit, a dielectric decrement improves the mean ionic activity coefficients (MIAC), whereas a Born term counts the solvation of the ions a second time and is therefore left out. The equation of state then adds only volume, dispersion and temperature parameters of the ions, fitted to aqueous MIAC and densities. openCOSMO-RS-ES-Phi reproduces COSMO-RS-ES in dilute aqueous solutions, improves on it in concentrated ones and also yields solution densities. Extrapolating from aqueous systems, it predicts the MIAC in water + cosolvent mixtures as accurately as the fitted COSMO-RS-ES, as well as the MIAC and bubble points of a benchmark database of water-alcohol-salt systems. Salting-out of organic components is not described as accurately, and salts come out too soluble in organic solvents. Overall, the interaction model developed for COSMO-RS-ES carries over to a large extent to an equation of state, which makes openCOSMO-RS-ES-Phi a sound base model for further development, with ion transfer between solvents as a clear target for fitting to non-aqueous data.

title: Multiplayer Stopping Games with a Conditionally Atomless Filtration
text:
Title: Multiplayer Stopping Games with a Conditionally Atomless Filtration
Domain: Optimization and Control (math.OC)

Stopping games are the multiplayer generalization of optimal stopping problems, in which each player independently chooses when to stop, and the payoff depends on who stops first and when. While the existence of $\varepsilon$-equilibria in two-player stopping games with integrable payoffs is known, the multiplayer case has remained open. We prove that every multiplayer stopping game in discrete time with integrable payoff process admits an $\varepsilon$-equilibrium for every $\varepsilon > 0$, provided the filtration is conditionally atomless. This condition is satisfied, in particular, when the underlying probability space is $\{0,1\}^{\dN}$ endowed with the uniform measure and its natural filtration. Our method also shows that every three-player stopping game, without the restriction to conditionally atomless filtration, admits an $\varepsilon$-equilibrium, for every $\varepsilon > 0$. The proof combines techniques developed for two-player stopping games and for multiplayer quitting games, with a key new insight: the richness encoded in a conditionally atomless filtration can substitute for an external public randomization device, allowing players to coordinate without an explicit coordination signal.

title: Surf_2_Volume: A Python Toolbox for Cortical Ribbon Based CIFTI to NIfTI Conversion
text:
Title: Surf_2_Volume: A Python Toolbox for Cortical Ribbon Based CIFTI to NIfTI Conversion
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Many neuroimaging workflows require NIfTI label volumes, whereas cortical parcellations are increasingly distributed in CIFTI surface space. Existing conversion tools offer several mapping settings. In nearest vertex mapping, a small distance can leave cortical voxels unlabeled, whereas a larger distance can extend labels beyond the intended cortical region. Choosing among settings is difficult when no paired volume atlas is available. We present Surf_2_Volume, a Python toolbox that projects discrete cortical labels within an adjustable cortical ribbon. Users can specify the ribbon threshold directly or use an optional procedure that ranks candidate thresholds using information from the source atlas. This procedure ranks 12 thresholds by differences between each label's proportion of source cortical vertices and its proportion of output voxels, without using a published volume atlas for selection. We evaluated four configurations from two atlas families: Yeo2011 parcellations with 7 and 17 networks, represented by 51 and 114 spatial components, and Schaefer2018 100-parcel atlases with 7 and 17 network assignments. All four selected sets included threshold 0.05, which had the highest macro-Dice and macro-Jaccard among the tested package thresholds. Eleven of the 12 selected outputs had higher macro-Dice than the best tested Connectome Workbench mapping for their atlas. In 24 HCP participants, all 12 selected outputs had higher participant-level mean parcel time-series concordance than every tested Workbench mapping (all within-atlas FDR-adjusted p < 0.001). Surf_2_Volume provides a reproducible way to generate and select volume atlas candidates when only a surface parcellation is available, while retaining alternatives for different coverage and signal-extraction needs.

title: Ultrafast Hole Transport and Electron Localization in Superatomic Re$_{6}$Se$_{8}$Cl$_{2}$
text:
Title: Ultrafast Hole Transport and Electron Localization in Superatomic Re$_{6}$Se$_{8}$Cl$_{2}$
Domain: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

Van der Waals superatomic crystals represent an intriguing class of materials, exhibiting unique ultrafast electronic and structural responses arising from their hierarchical crystal structure. These materials bridge the properties of semiconductors, molecular solids, and nanocrystal arrays, hosting a range of many-body interactions that can be controlled with atomically precise structures. To establish the structure-function correlation, it is necessary to understand element-specific electronic states arising from complex superatomic unit cells. Here, we use transient XUV spectroscopy to individually probe the dynamics of photoexcited electrons and holes in Re$_{6}$Se$_{8}$Cl$_{2}$ superatomic crystals. We simultaneously measure photodynamics at the Re O$_{2}$ and Se M$_{4,5}$ edges, enabling decomposition of excited-state dynamics into the contributions of electron, hole, band gap, and phonon dynamics occurring around Re and Se atoms. By correlating spectral features at the Re and Se edges, we infer the existence of flat conduction bands and identify hot hole transfer from Re to Se atoms. We observe phonon oscillations driven by hole-mediated displacive excitations. The measurements highlight that the photodynamics are dominated by charge transfer between metallic sites which drives phonon coupling in the nonequilibrium state. This work provides insights into the optoelectronic applications of superatomic crystals for future tuning of emergent material properties.

title: TargetAgent: Mathematical AI Co-Scientist for Drug Target Identification
text:
Title: TargetAgent: Mathematical AI Co-Scientist for Drug Target Identification
Domain: Quantitative Methods in Biology (q-bio.QM)

Given the challenges of pharmaceutical development, there is increasing interest in computational approaches for identifying novel drug targets. Transcriptomics technologies enable the analysis of disease mechanisms at unprecedented resolution, while spatially resolved platforms further preserve the spatial organization of cells within tissues, allowing analysis to focus on specific regions of disease localization. To derive actionable therapeutic targets from these data, it is necessary to identify mechanisms that recur across a population rather than those observed in individual patients, which requires integrated analysis across disease conditions and donor cohorts. Here, we present the groundwork for an AI co-scientist framework for the sequential analysis of multi-batch spatial transcriptomics data that integrates interpretable mathematical models, including optimal transport, tensor factorizations, and topological data analysis, with LLM-powered agentic interpretation. Leveraging the complementary information provided by these mathematical models, the agents sequentially identify regions in which the disease is localized, molecular targets within these regions, and the direction in which each target should be modulated. Applied as a proof of concept to a public Stereo-seq study of the Alzheimer's disease (AD)-affected prefrontal cortex, we demonstrate that the agents converge on the white matter as the primary locus of the moderate-disease signal and identify a loss of myelin programme usage despite increasing oligodendrocyte abundance. The agents subsequently propose 29 candidate therapeutic targets, led by an oligodendrocyte differentiation module on which multiple mathematical perspectives converge, and flag 20 genes whose relevance to AD has not been previously reported. These results are hypothesis-generating and motivate further validation in larger, independent cohorts.
